checks.name: a5-live-local-exercise-passes-with-zero-skips
checks.summary: Real process, real emulator, real HTTP, 0 skips (G7): scripts/firestore-emulator.sh starts firebase-tools 15.27.0's Firestore emulator (a free TCP port, polled for readiness, torn down on exit) and exports FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST for the go test child. The test go-builds cmd/control-plane into a temp binary and starts it as a real OS process (runner.ProcessSupervisor, its own process group) with AGENTIC_LOOP_ALLOW_FIRESTORE_EMULATOR=1 and AGENTIC_LOOP_LOCAL_OWNER_TOKENS=<token>=owner@example.com, polling /healthz on a 20s bounded deadline (no fixed sleep). Observed over real HTTP: POST /v1/requirements with no bearer token -> 401, with an unknown bearer token -> 401, then with the correct bearer token -> 201 (capture, requirement_id=requirement-7cd5a21be38e95f9-1); GET /v1/requirements shows it in the Backlog; GET /v1/requirements/{id} (Requirement view) returns original_text and status=captured; POST /v1/controls (scope_kind=installation, mode=allow) -> 200 revision=1; GET /v1/controls (Control view) shows it; GET /v1/export?format=json includes a requirement record for the same id. Direct emulator reads (cloudfirestore client connected straight to FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, bypassing this app's HTTP API entirely) confirmed real Firestore documents with no GitHub Issue involved: requirements=1, controls=1, events=2, outbox=1, quota=1 documents for this run's installation. The first control-plane process was then stopped and a second, freshly-built process started against the same emulator/installation; GET /v1/requirements/{id} and GET /v1/controls on the new process still returned the same data, proving persistence lives in Firestore, not process memory. PASS in 10.42s total (including the go build step); test log line: 'PASS: TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive (10.42s)'.

checks.name: a6-budget-hard-guard-429-before-side-effect
checks.summary: Same run as a5, its last phase: real POST /v1/requirements capture calls repeated against the live process (each a full HTTP round trip and a real Firestore emulator mutation transaction) until internal/quota.DefaultBudget's write ceiling (10,000/day, V2-013's 50% hard budget) tripped. The worst-case reservation (internal/quota.MutationUsage.Writes=16) is checked and refused in internal/store/firestore.unit.ReserveQuota before any document is staged, so no partial mutation from the refused call is ever written; the true-up after each successful call corrects the running total down to its real ~5-write cost, which is why exhaustion took 1,994 real successful mutations, not 625. Observed: the 1995th capture returned HTTP 429 with body error=quota_exhausted (never 400) and a Retry-After header naming the next UTC midnight (Wed, 26 Aug 2026 00:00:00 GMT). Log line: 'budget hard guard tripped as HTTP 429 quota_exhausted after 1994 real capture mutations in 9.050858732s'.
